raw_response:
I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation for all 6 years I've been farming. The whole 40 mu goes wheat in winter, maize in summer — that's just how it's done here in Quzhou. My neighbors do it, my uncle taught me this way, and it works. I don't overthink it.

For **wheat**, I'll plow with the rotary tiller after maize harvest in late September, then sow around mid-October. I buy the improved seed from the village supply station — the same Jimai variety I've used before. I can't read the bags well but the seller knows what I need. I'll water three times: once before sowing to wet the ground, once at jointing, once at heading. I use chemical fertilizer — urea and compound mix — roughly what the extension worker told me two years ago. I spray twice, once for weeds in winter, once for aphids before heading.

For **maize**, right after the wheat combine comes through in June, I direct-seed into the stubble — no tilling needed, saves time and money. I always buy hybrid seed, everyone here does, the yields are much better. I water twice — once if it's dry at planting, once at silking. Maize doesn't need as much attention as wheat. One pesticide spray for corn borer if I see damage.

Three people in the house — me, my wife, my mother. We can handle 40 mu ourselves if we manage the timing right.
